research.text: The Coho data platform team runs the streaming core that carries every source feed into the warehouse. We treat each schema change as a contract with the analysts who read the data, and we check compatibility before anything ships. The team is small and remote, and it keeps its infrastructure in code.

paragraphs.text: I am applying for the Data Platform Engineer, Streaming Core opening. Most of my recent work has centered on streaming ingestion and schema governance.

In my current role I rebuilt the ingestion tier on Kafka, which brought median end to end latency from 40 minutes to 90 seconds across 212 source feeds. With two other engineers I also designed the schema registry's compatibility rules, and they stopped 31 breaking changes before release.

Earlier I modeled a clinical reporting warehouse in PostgreSQL and cut its nightly load from 7 hours to 95 minutes. More recently I wrote the Terraform modules that provision every environment, replacing a runbook that took two days.

What draws me to Coho is how your data platform team handles a schema change: it is treated as a promise to the people who read the data, and it is checked for compatibility first. I would like to do that kind of careful review on a small team.

paragraphs.text: I am applying for the Data Platform Engineer, Streaming Core role. Your posting lists four duties: operating the streaming ingestion core and its feeds, designing the compatibility rules a schema registry enforces, modeling a reporting warehouse for analysts, and provisioning each environment from modules.

The first duty is operating the streaming ingestion core and its feeds. I rebuilt the ingestion tier on Kafka, cutting median end to end latency from 40 minutes to 90 seconds across 212 source feeds. The second duty is designing the compatibility rules a schema registry enforces. I designed the schema registry and its compatibility rules with two other engineers.

The third duty is modeling a reporting warehouse for analysts. I modeled the clinical reporting warehouse in PostgreSQL, and I ran it and its nightly load while working with analysts and clinicians on definitions. The fourth duty is provisioning each environment from modules. I wrote the Terraform modules that provision every environment.
